subject.title: fix(agents): treat unterminated Responses SSE stream as error, not success

question: Should every provider configured with `api: "openai-responses"`, including custom and proxy endpoints, be required to emit `response.completed`, `response.incomplete`, or `response.failed`, and should this PR be the canonical implementation?
rationale: Failing plain EOF fixes silent message loss but deliberately removes compatibility with non-conformant providers, while the competing PR exposes the failure at a different internal boundary.

options.title: Enforce the Responses contract
options.body: Require terminal events for all Responses-compatible providers, rebase and land this proof-positive branch, and close the competing PR.

options.title: Preserve non-conformant providers
options.body: Revise the patch with an owner-approved capability or compatibility policy before making plain EOF fatal.

options.title: Choose the direct-throw branch
options.body: Use the competing PR if maintainers want processResponsesStream itself to throw rather than returning an error outcome to the existing caller guard.

recommendation.title: Enforce the Responses contract
recommendation.body: Require terminal events for all Responses-compatible providers, rebase and land this proof-positive branch, and close the competing PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this person to Responses transport timeout and error-outcome behavior.
